Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a soft tissue opacity at the right lung apex (indicated by the arrow) with associated destruction/erosion of the adjacent first and second ribs. In an elderly patient with a history of long-term smoking, this apical mass with rib invasion is characteristic of a Pancoast tumour (superior sulcus tumour).
